### Observed differences

- In the later window, A27 is present in about 99 in 100 traces, up from about 61 in 100, and occurs about once per trace where present (mean occurrences per trace 1.0 versus 0.61). [OCC002]
- The four activities A32, A33, A38 and A39, each previously seen in about 39 in 100 traces, are now observed in only about 1–2 in 100 traces. [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- A26's outgoing transitions now lead to A27 in about 97 in 100 cases (previously about 60 in 100), and A26 precedes A27 in about 97 in 100 traces (previously 61 in 100). [DIR003, REL006]
- The A27–A28 sequence tightened: the two now co-occur in about 99 in 100 traces with A27 first in about 98 in 100, and A28 falls exactly two event positions after A26 in about 98 in 100 traces, whereas before it did so in 61 in 100 and sat five positions after A26 in about 37 in 100. [REL011, LAG001]
- A10 is executed more often and later in the trace: participation rose from about 8 to about 25 in 100 traces, and its mean relative position moved from 0.62 to 0.81. [OCC001, POS001]
- A10's surroundings changed: about 88 in 100 of its outgoing transitions now go to A46 (previously about 29 in 100), it immediately follows A45 in about 70 in 100 of the observed A45–A10 pairs (44 later-window observations, up from 7), and A45's transitions to A10 rose from about 3 to about 26 in 100. [DIR001, LAG009, DIR006]
- A45 and A46 now appear in about 64 in 100 traces (previously about 39) and co-occur with A27 in about 63 in 100 traces (previously 35), rarely appearing without A27 (about 1 in 100, previously 23 in 100). [REL016, REL017, REL025, REL026]
- A11's outgoing split shifted from A12 towards A13 (about 40 and 22 in 100 transitions before, about 21 and 40 in 100 after). [DIR002]
- The later-window outgoing and lag profiles of the now-rare activities A32, A33, A38 and A39 rest on only 2–3 observations each and are too thin to characterise any new routing. [DIR004, DIR005, LAG002, LAG005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the process now runs a single dominant path in which A26 is followed by A27 and then A28, with A28 two event positions after A26, while the block of activities A32, A33, A38 and A39 that previously executed between A26 and A28 in roughly four in ten cases is now largely skipped; in addition, A10 appears in about a quarter of later-window cases, late in the flow, typically chained between A45 and A46. Sixty-four qualifying items stand against roughly 0.82 expected if nothing had changed, and the ordering evidence is direct rather than inferential: A26 precedes A27 in about 97 in 100 later-window traces, A27 precedes A28 in about 98 in 100, A28 sits at lag 2 after A26 in about 98 in 100, and the four branch activities fall from 78–79 supporting traces to 2–3, with occurrence, routing, position, relation and lag indicators all describing the same restructuring. [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, DIR003, REL006, REL011, LAG001]

Limitations: the four activities still appear in 2–3 later-window traces, so the evidence cannot distinguish complete removal from a residual low-frequency branch, and their remaining routing and lag profiles rest on 2–3 observations; the A10–A45–A46 chain is quantified on roughly 44–50 later-window observations, leaving its exact share uncertain; and the A11 shift from A12 towards A13 is not tied into the main restructuring by any observed relation. The main competing explanation is a sampling-driven shift in variant frequencies — the A27 path already existed before, so the later window could in principle under-represent the A32/A33/A38/A39 variants — but a drop from about 39 to about 1 in 100 traces across four activities, consistently reflected in routing, co-occurrence and lag measures, is difficult to attribute to sampling variation alone. [OCC002, DIR002, DIR004, LAG005, LAG009]
